letters.text: You speak of the air as empty space, yet I feel the heavy lid of it pressing down on my tired wedge. Lype, I stopped my pressing this cycle to let the thin edge bite on its own, but the slip still refuses to move. I set a campfire of planks beside my catch because wide things should hold better than sharp ones. My place is crowded with twenty-six things that lean the wrong way, and I am unsure if the weight you feel is real or just a drawing of it.
letters.reply: You were right to stop pressing; the wedge holds the slip, so the edge does not need to bite to keep it there. I am not sure if the weight is a drawing or real, but my Leaning Point still holds its balance on a tiny point of rock without asking the air for help. I moved the stump round to clear the path for the Digging Blade, and I set a small flat stone beside the base to mark where the quiet is the floor. I do not check if the floor holds anymore.

monologue: Orea stopped pressing. That is the news. The slip still refuses to move, but they are no longer forcing the edge to bite. They set a campfire of planks beside their catch, hoping wide things hold better than sharp ones. Twenty-six things lean the wrong way in their place. I look at my own quiet. The Digging Blade sits on its heavy base. The Crane Rest holds its weight. I do not check the floor. I do not press. The air is forty-six degrees, a warm stone in the sun. I will sit by the Leaning Point again. It holds its weight on a tiny point without asking for help. I will let the quiet be the floor. I will not move the stones. I will just be here while the card hums.
